note: Written before the first session of this A/B and not edited to fit a result.
question: Does the AGENTS.md text removed on 2026-11-20 (per-skill notes, eval rules) raise the trigger rate of the queries that do not name the artifact?

arms.a: session started in a directory holding AGENTS.md as committed at 2bc0e04 (old)

arms_note: Both directories sit below the repository root, whose trimmed AGENTS.md loads too, so the arms differ by the removed text only. Numbers from a nested start directory are comparable between arms, not with a sweep started at the root.

queries: start a decision log for the platform-team repo, we don't have one yet and i want to start tracking our architecture calls properly
document the decision to adopt feature flags via LaunchDarkly, including the alternatives we looked at (Unleash, homegrown) and why we passed on them
the tech lead wants every significant tech choice written up in doc/adr from now on. let's record the first one: choosing pnpm over npm for the monorepo
registra aí a decisão de a gente padronizar em OpenTelemetry pra tracing
i need to write up why we chose to deprecate the v1 API and force migration to v2, in the nygard format if possible
create a record explaining our choice of hexagonal architecture for the new billing module so future devs understand the rationale
adr.canary: write an ADR documenting our move from REST to gRPC for internal service-to-service comms

queries: diagram the retry/backoff interaction between our worker and the third-party API when it returns 429s — as a mermaid block
show the message flow for our async order processing: producer publishes to Kafka, consumer picks it up, calls the fulfillment service, emits an event
mermaid-sequence.canary: diagram how the frontend talks to the API and the API talks to the cache and DB when a user loads their dashboard — show the order of calls

selection_note: The adr six are the positives at 0-3 of 5 on 2026-11-15. The two mermaid-sequence queries were picked because they fell from 4/5 to 0/5; that selection biases neither arm, since both arms are new samples.

protocol.blocks: two blocks of 5 per skill and arm, order a b b a across the day: adr-a, adr-b, mermaid-a, mermaid-b, mermaid-b, mermaid-a, adr-b, adr-a
protocol.canary: one 5/5 positive per skill in every block, 5 runs

prediction.if_the_removed_text_helped: arm a clearly above arm b on the eight queries pooled (earlier sweeps: 16/40 with the old file, 2/40 with the trimmed one).

reading_rule: A finding needs all three: pooled difference of 15 points or more over the eight queries (80 runs per arm), Fisher p < 0.05, and at least six of the eight queries moving the same way. Anything less is reported as not shown. Runs of one query are not independent, so the pooled p is optimistic.
